diagnosis.original_evidence: The packaged R26+HUD R30 semanticWorld classifier checked CurrentDrawMatchesVerifiedWorld and R28CanRebindVerifiedWorld before asking R30GetExactLensCentreRawWvp whether the C993 sun itself owned the original c64. The shared lower R26 R28CanRebindVerifiedWorld also admitted WorldBillboard, so a stale prior world owner could supersede the centre-specific route.
diagnosis.root_cause: A previous verified world shader/epoch was allowed to select the renderer owner before the exact central sun source proof, despite game raw c64 having different object provenance. This is a code-confirmed ownership-order defect, not a hardware-proven optical symptom.
alternatives_rejected: Do not simply increase c64 draw-age threshold or reuse live already-adjusted GPU constants.
Do not delete/reclassify outer CABE flares, suppress alpha, change SkyGlow, or loosen all WorldBillboard ownership.
A static ordering repair and Windows CI do not themselves confirm Quest3 binocular appearance.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: R30 source-owned centre route now precedes historical verified-world and R28 rebind, with lower R26 rebind guard. The existing C993 raw c64 and pose/shader evidence predicate remains intact.
diagnosis.negative_test_evidence: Header compile-time route assertions and portable smoke check exact owned, stale pose, shader change, outer ring, and queued fallback; hardware test pending.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: Exact owned centre reaches existing R26+HUD headInverse/eyeInverse/eyeProjection pipeline; missing source is left to original game drawing without unrelated old shader rebind.

runtime_evidence: Quest3/VDXR and actual OutRun game display were not tested; CI alone is insufficient to assert central flare convergence.
